#### pub fn [as_borrowed](https://docs.rs#method.as_borrowed)(&self) -> [CodePointMapDataBorrowed](https://docs.rs/struct.CodePointMapDataBorrowed.html)<'_, T>

Construct a borrowed version of this type that can be queried.

This avoids a potential small underlying cost per API call (like `get()`) by consolidating it
up front.

This owned version if returned by functions that use a runtime data provider.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/icu_properties/code_point_map.rs.html#104-111)#### pub fn [try_into_converted](https://docs.rs#method.try_into_converted)<P>(self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[CodePointMapData](https://docs.rs/struct.CodePointMapData.html)<P>, [UleError](https://docs.rs/zerovec/0.11.6/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/zerovec/ule/enum.UleError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/icu_properties/code_point_map.rs.html#104-111)

#### pub fn [try_into_converted](https://docs.rs#method.try_into_converted)<P>(self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[CodePointMapData](https://docs.rs/struct.CodePointMapData.html)<P>, [UleError](https://docs.rs/zerovec/0.11.6/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/zerovec/ule/enum.UleError.html)>

Convert this map to a map around another type

Typically useful for type-erasing maps into maps around integers.

✨ *Enabled with the  alloc Cargo feature.*

[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

Will panic if T and P are different sizes

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use icu::properties::CodePointMapData;
use icu::properties::props::GeneralCategory;
let data = CodePointMapData::<GeneralCategory>::new().static_to_owned();
let gc = data.try_into_converted::<u8>().unwrap();
let gc = gc.as_borrowed();
assert_eq!(gc.get('木'), GeneralCategory::OtherLetter as u8);  // U+6728
assert_eq!(gc.get('🎃'), GeneralCategory::OtherSymbol as u8);  // U+1F383 JACK-O-LANTERN
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/icu_properties/code_point_map.rs.html#140-142)#### pub fn [as_code_point_trie](https://docs.rs#method.as_code_point_trie)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[CodePointTrie](https://docs.rs/icu_collections/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_collections/codepointtrie/cptrie/struct.CodePointTrie.html)<'_, T>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/icu_properties/code_point_map.rs.html#140-142)

#### pub fn [as_code_point_trie](https://docs.rs#method.as_code_point_trie)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[CodePointTrie](https://docs.rs/icu_collections/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_collections/codepointtrie/cptrie/struct.CodePointTrie.html)<'_, T>>

Convert this type to a [ CodePointTrie](https://docs.rs/icu_collections/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_collections/codepointtrie/cptrie/struct.CodePointTrie.html) as a borrowed value.

The data backing this is extensible and supports multiple implementations.
Currently it is always [ CodePointTrie](https://docs.rs/icu_collections/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_collections/codepointtrie/cptrie/struct.CodePointTrie.html); however in the future more backends may be
added, and users may select which at data generation time.

This method returns an `Option` in order to return `None` when the backing data provider
cannot return a [ CodePointTrie](https://docs.rs/icu_collections/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_collections/codepointtrie/cptrie/struct.CodePointTrie.html), or cannot do so within the expected constant time
constraint.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/icu_properties/code_point_map.rs.html#153-155)#### pub fn [to_code_point_trie](https://docs.rs#method.to_code_point_trie)(&self) -> [CodePointTrie](https://docs.rs/icu_collections/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_collections/codepointtrie/cptrie/struct.CodePointTrie.html)<'_, T>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/icu_properties/code_point_map.rs.html#153-155)

#### pub fn [to_code_point_trie](https://docs.rs#method.to_code_point_trie)(&self) -> [CodePointTrie](https://docs.rs/icu_collections/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_collections/codepointtrie/cptrie/struct.CodePointTrie.html)<'_, T>

Convert this type to a [ CodePointTrie](https://docs.rs/icu_collections/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_collections/codepointtrie/cptrie/struct.CodePointTrie.html), borrowing if possible,
otherwise allocating a new

[.](https://docs.rs/icu_collections/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_collections/codepointtrie/cptrie/struct.CodePointTrie.html)

`CodePointTrie`The data backing this is extensible and supports multiple implementations.
Currently it is always [ CodePointTrie](https://docs.rs/icu_collections/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_collections/codepointtrie/cptrie/struct.CodePointTrie.html); however in the future more backends may be
added, and users may select which at data generation time.

The performance of the conversion to this specific return type will vary
depending on the data structure that is backing `self`.

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/icu_properties/bidi.rs.html#121-125)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-BidiDataSource-for-CodePointMapDataBorrowed%3C'_,+BidiClass%3E)### impl [BidiDataSource](https://docs.rs/unicode-bidi/0.3.18/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/unicode_bidi/data_source/trait.BidiDataSource.html) for [CodePointMapDataBorrowed](https://docs.rs/struct.CodePointMapDataBorrowed.html)<'_, [BidiClass](https://docs.rs/props/struct.BidiClass.html)>

Available on **crate feature **`unicode_bidi` only.✨ *Enabled with the *`unicode_bidi` Cargo feature.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/icu_properties/bidi.rs.html#121-125)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-BidiDataSource-for-CodePointMapDataBorrowed%3C'_,+BidiClass%3E)

### impl [BidiDataSource](https://docs.rs/unicode-bidi/0.3.18/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/unicode_bidi/data_source/trait.BidiDataSource.html) for [CodePointMapDataBorrowed](https://docs.rs/struct.CodePointMapDataBorrowed.html)<'_, [BidiClass](https://docs.rs/props/struct.BidiClass.html)>

**crate feature**only.

`unicode_bidi`✨ *Enabled with the  unicode_bidi Cargo feature.*

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-3)Examples

```
 use icu::properties::CodePointMapData;
 use icu::properties::props::BidiClass;
 use unicode_bidi::BidiInfo;
 // This example text is defined using `concat!` because some browsers
 // and text editors have trouble displaying bidi strings.
 let text =  concat!["א", // RTL#1
                     "ב", // RTL#2
                     "ג", // RTL#3
                     "a", // LTR#1
                     "b", // LTR#2
                     "c", // LTR#3
                     ]; //
 let bidi_map = CodePointMapData::<BidiClass>::new();
 // Resolve embedding levels within the text.  Pass `None` to detect the
 // paragraph level automatically.
 let bidi_info = BidiInfo::new_with_data_source(&bidi_map, text, None);
 // This paragraph has embedding level 1 because its first strong character is RTL.
 assert_eq!(bidi_info.paragraphs.len(), 1);
 let para = &bidi_info.paragraphs[0];
 assert_eq!(para.level.number(), 1);
 assert!(para.level.is_rtl());
 // Re-ordering is done after wrapping each paragraph into a sequence of
 // lines. For this example, I'll just use a single line that spans the
 // entire paragraph.
 let line = para.range.clone();
 let display = bidi_info.reorder_line(para, line);
 assert_eq!(display, concat!["a", // LTR#1
                             "b", // LTR#2
                             "c", // LTR#3
                             "ג", // RTL#3
                             "ב", // RTL#2
                             "א", // RTL#1
                             ]);
```

### impl<'a> [CodePointSetDataBorrowed](https://docs.rs/struct.CodePointSetDataBorrowed.html)<'a>

Check if the set contains a character

```
use icu::properties::CodePointSetData;
use icu::properties::props::Alphabetic;
let alphabetic = CodePointSetData::new::<Alphabetic>();
assert!(!alphabetic.contains('3'));
assert!(!alphabetic.contains('੩'));  // U+0A69 GURMUKHI DIGIT THREE
assert!(alphabetic.contains('A'));
assert!(alphabetic.contains('Ä'));  // U+00C4 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER A WITH DIAERESIS
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/icu_properties/code_point_set.rs.html#190-192)#### pub fn [iter_ranges](https://docs.rs#method.iter_ranges)(self) -> impl [Iterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html)<Item = [RangeInclusive](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/range/struct.RangeInclusive.html)<[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)>> + 'a

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/icu_properties/code_point_set.rs.html#190-192)

#### pub fn [iter_ranges](https://docs.rs#method.iter_ranges)(self) -> impl [Iterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html)<Item = [RangeInclusive](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/range/struct.RangeInclusive.html)<[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)>> + 'a

included in the `CodePointSetData`

Ranges are returned as [ RangeInclusive](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/range/struct.RangeInclusive.html), which is inclusive of its

`end` bound value. An end-inclusive behavior matches the ICU4C/J
behavior of ranges, ex: `UnicodeSet::contains(UChar32 start, UChar32 end)`.[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use icu::properties::props::Alphabetic;
use icu::properties::CodePointSetData;
let alphabetic = CodePointSetData::new::<Alphabetic>();
let mut ranges = alphabetic.iter_ranges();
assert_eq!(Some(0x0041..=0x005A), ranges.next()); // 'A'..'Z'
assert_eq!(Some(0x0061..=0x007A), ranges.next()); // 'a'..'z'
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/icu_properties/code_point_set.rs.html#214-216)#### pub fn [iter_ranges_complemented](https://docs.rs#method.iter_ranges_complemented)(

A version of `new()` that uses custom data provided by a [ DataProvider](https://docs.rs/icu_provider/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_provider/data_provider/trait.DataProvider.html).

Note that this will return an owned version of the data. Functionality is available on
the borrowed version, accessible through [ EmojiSetData::as_borrowed](https://docs.rs/struct.EmojiSetData.html#method.as_borrowed).

This avoids a potential small underlying cost per API call (ex: `contains()`) by consolidating it
up front.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/icu_properties/emoji.rs.html#91-95)#### pub fn [as_code_point_inversion_list_string_list](https://docs.rs#method.as_code_point_inversion_list_string_list)(
    &self,
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[CodePointInversionListAndStringList](https://docs.rs/icu_collections/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_collections/codepointinvliststringlist/struct.CodePointInversionListAndStringList.html)<'_>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/icu_properties/emoji.rs.html#91-95)

#### pub fn [as_code_point_inversion_list_string_list](https://docs.rs#method.as_code_point_inversion_list_string_list)(
    &self,
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[CodePointInversionListAndStringList](https://docs.rs/icu_collections/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_collections/codepointinvliststringlist/struct.CodePointInversionListAndStringList.html)<'_>>

Convert this type to a [ CodePointInversionListAndStringList](https://docs.rs/icu_collections/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_collections/codepointinvliststringlist/struct.CodePointInversionListAndStringList.html) as a borrowed value.

The data backing this is extensible and supports multiple implementations.
Currently it is always [ CodePointInversionListAndStringList](https://docs.rs/icu_collections/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_collections/codepointinvliststringlist/struct.CodePointInversionListAndStringList.html); however in the future more backends may be
added, and users may select which at data generation time.

This method returns an `Option` in order to return `None` when the backing data provider
cannot return a [ CodePointInversionListAndStringList](https://docs.rs/icu_collections/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_collections/codepointinvliststringlist/struct.CodePointInversionListAndStringList.html), or cannot do so within the expected constant time
constraint.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/icu_properties/emoji.rs.html#106-110)#### pub fn [to_code_point_inversion_list_string_list](https://docs.rs#method.to_code_point_inversion_list_string_list)(
    &self,
) -> [CodePointInversionListAndStringList](https://docs.rs/icu_collections/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_collections/codepointinvliststringlist/struct.CodePointInversionListAndStringList.html)<'_>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/icu_properties/emoji.rs.html#106-110)

#### pub fn [to_code_point_inversion_list_string_list](https://docs.rs#method.to_code_point_inversion_list_string_list)(
    &self,
) -> [CodePointInversionListAndStringList](https://docs.rs/icu_collections/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_collections/codepointinvliststringlist/struct.CodePointInversionListAndStringList.html)<'_>

Convert this type to a [ CodePointInversionListAndStringList](https://docs.rs/icu_collections/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_collections/codepointinvliststringlist/struct.CodePointInversionListAndStringList.html), borrowing if possible,
otherwise allocating a new

[.](https://docs.rs/icu_collections/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_collections/codepointinvliststringlist/struct.CodePointInversionListAndStringList.html)

`CodePointInversionListAndStringList`The data backing this is extensible and supports multiple implementations.
Currently it is always [ CodePointInversionListAndStringList](https://docs.rs/icu_collections/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_collections/codepointinvliststringlist/struct.CodePointInversionListAndStringList.html); however in the future more backends may be
added, and users may select which at data generation time.

The performance of the conversion to this specific return type will vary
depending on the data structure that is backing `self`.

# PropertyNamesLong in icu_properties - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/icu_properties/^2.2/struct.PropertyNamesLong.html

`pub struct PropertyNamesLong<T: `[NamedEnumeratedProperty](https://docs.rs/props/trait.NamedEnumeratedProperty.html)> { /* private fields */ }## Expand description

A struct capable of looking up a property name from a value
Access its data by calling [ Self::as_borrowed()](https://docs.rs/struct.PropertyNamesLong.html#method.as_borrowed) and using the methods on

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.PropertyNamesLongBorrowed.html)

`PropertyNamesLongBorrowed`[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use icu::properties::props::CanonicalCombiningClass;
use icu::properties::PropertyNamesLong;
let names = PropertyNamesLong::<CanonicalCombiningClass>::new();
assert_eq!(
    names.get(CanonicalCombiningClass::KanaVoicing),
    Some("Kana_Voicing")
);
assert_eq!(
    names.get(CanonicalCombiningClass::AboveLeft),
    Some("Above_Left")
);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/icu_properties/names.rs.html#631-634)#### pub fn [get_locale_script](https://docs.rs#method.get_locale_script)(self, property: [Script](https://docs.rs/props/struct.Script.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Script](https://docs.rs/icu_locale_core/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_locale_core/subtags/script/struct.Script.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/icu_properties/names.rs.html#631-634)

#### pub fn [get_locale_script](https://docs.rs#method.get_locale_script)(self, property: [Script](https://docs.rs/props/struct.Script.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Script](https://docs.rs/icu_locale_core/2.2.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/icu_locale_core/subtags/script/struct.Script.html)>

Gets the “name” of a script property as a `icu::locale::subtags::Script`.

This method is available only on `PropertyNamesShortBorrowed<Script>`.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

```
use icu::locale::subtags::script;
use icu::properties::props::Script;
use icu::properties::PropertyNamesShort;
let lookup = PropertyNamesShort::<Script>::new();
assert_eq!(
    lookup.get_locale_script(Script::Brahmi),
    Some(script!("Brah"))
);
assert_eq!(
    lookup.get_locale_script(Script::Hangul),
    Some(script!("Hang"))
);
```
For the reverse direction, use property parsing as normal:

```
use icu::locale::subtags::script;
use icu::properties::props::Script;
use icu::properties::PropertyParser;
let parser = PropertyParser::<Script>::new();
assert_eq!(
    parser.get_strict(script!("Brah").as_str()),
    Some(Script::Brahmi)
);
assert_eq!(
    parser.get_strict(script!("Hang").as_str()),
    Some(Script::Hangul)
);
```

Cheaply converts a [ PropertyNamesShortBorrowed<'static>](https://docs.rs/struct.PropertyNamesShortBorrowed.html) into a

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.PropertyNamesShort.html)

`PropertyNamesShort`Note: Due to branching and indirection, using [ PropertyNamesShort](https://docs.rs/struct.PropertyNamesShort.html) might inhibit some
compile-time optimizations that are possible with

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.PropertyNamesShortBorrowed.html)

`PropertyNamesShortBorrowed`This is currently not `const` unlike other `static_to_owned()` functions since it needs
const traits to do that safely

# PropertyParser in icu_properties - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/icu_properties/^2.2/struct.PropertyParser.html

`pub struct PropertyParser<T> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A struct capable of looking up a property value from a string name.
Access its data by calling [ Self::as_borrowed()](https://docs.rs/struct.PropertyParser.html#method.as_borrowed) and using the methods on

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.PropertyParserBorrowed.html)

`PropertyParserBorrowed`The name can be a short name (`Lu`), a long name(`Uppercase_Letter`),
or an alias.

Property names can be looked up using “strict” matching (looking for a name that matches exactly), or “loose matching”, where the name is allowed to deviate in terms of ASCII casing, whitespace, underscores, and hyphens.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use icu::properties::props::GeneralCategory;
use icu::properties::PropertyParser;
let lookup = PropertyParser::<GeneralCategory>::new();
// short name for value
assert_eq!(
    lookup.get_strict("Lu"),
    Some(GeneralCategory::UppercaseLetter)
);
assert_eq!(
    lookup.get_strict("Pd"),
    Some(GeneralCategory::DashPunctuation)
);
// long name for value
assert_eq!(
    lookup.get_strict("Uppercase_Letter"),
    Some(GeneralCategory::UppercaseLetter)
);
assert_eq!(
    lookup.get_strict("Dash_Punctuation"),
    Some(GeneralCategory::DashPunctuation)
);
// name has incorrect casing
assert_eq!(lookup.get_strict("dashpunctuation"), None);
// loose matching of name
assert_eq!(
    lookup.get_loose("dash-punctuation"),
    Some(GeneralCategory::DashPunctuation)
);
// fake property
assert_eq!(lookup.get_strict("Animated_Gif"), None);
```

Get the property value as a u16, doing a strict search looking for names that match exactly

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use icu::properties::props::GeneralCategory;
use icu::properties::PropertyParser;
let lookup = PropertyParser::<GeneralCategory>::new();
assert_eq!(
    lookup.get_strict_u16("Lu"),
    Some(GeneralCategory::UppercaseLetter as u16)
);
assert_eq!(
    lookup.get_strict_u16("Uppercase_Letter"),
    Some(GeneralCategory::UppercaseLetter as u16)
);
// does not do loose matching
assert_eq!(lookup.get_strict_u16("UppercaseLetter"), None);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/icu_properties/names.rs.html#219-221)#### pub fn [get_loose_u16](https://docs.rs#method.get_loose_u16)(self, name: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/icu_properties/names.rs.html#219-221)

#### pub fn [get_loose_u16](https://docs.rs#method.get_loose_u16)(self, name: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)>

Get the property value as a u16, doing a loose search looking for names that match case-insensitively, ignoring ASCII hyphens, underscores, and whitespaces.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-2)Example

```
use icu::properties::props::GeneralCategory;
use icu::properties::PropertyParser;
let lookup = PropertyParser::<GeneralCategory>::new();
assert_eq!(
    lookup.get_loose_u16("Lu"),
    Some(GeneralCategory::UppercaseLetter as u16)
);
assert_eq!(
    lookup.get_loose_u16("Uppercase_Letter"),
    Some(GeneralCategory::UppercaseLetter as u16)
);
// does do loose matching
assert_eq!(
    lookup.get_loose_u16("UppercaseLetter"),
    Some(GeneralCategory::UppercaseLetter as u16)
);
```
Get the property value as a `T`, doing a loose search looking for
names that match case-insensitively, ignoring ASCII hyphens, underscores, and
whitespaces.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-3)Example

```
use icu::properties::props::GeneralCategory;
use icu::properties::PropertyParser;
let lookup = PropertyParser::<GeneralCategory>::new();
assert_eq!(
    lookup.get_loose("Lu"),
    Some(GeneralCategory::UppercaseLetter)
);
assert_eq!(
    lookup.get_loose("Uppercase_Letter"),
    Some(GeneralCategory::UppercaseLetter)
);
// does do loose matching
assert_eq!(
    lookup.get_loose("UppercaseLetter"),
    Some(GeneralCategory::UppercaseLetter)
);
```

#### pub const fn [static_to_owned](https://docs.rs#method.static_to_owned)(self) -> [PropertyParser](https://docs.rs/struct.PropertyParser.html)<T>

Cheaply converts a [ PropertyParserBorrowed<'static>](https://docs.rs/struct.PropertyParserBorrowed.html) into a

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.PropertyParser.html)

`PropertyParser`Note: Due to branching and indirection, using [ PropertyParser](https://docs.rs/struct.PropertyParser.html) might inhibit some
compile-time optimizations that are possible with

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.PropertyParserBorrowed.html)

# idna_adapter - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/idna_adapter/1.2.2/aarch64-apple-darwin/idna_adapter/

## Expand description

This crate abstracts over a Unicode back end for the [ idna](https://docs.rs/crate/idna/latest)
crate.

To work around the lack of [ global-features](https://internals.rust-lang.org/t/pre-rfc-mutually-excusive-global-features/19618) in Cargo, this
crate allows the top level

`Cargo.lock` to choose an alternative
Unicode back end for the `idna` crate by pinning a version of this
crate.See the [README of the latest version](https://docs.rs/crate/idna_adapter/latest) for more details.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Adapter](https://docs.rs/struct.Adapter.html)
- An adapter between a Unicode back end an the `idna`crate.
- [Bidi](https://docs.rs/struct.BidiClass.html)- Class
- Value for the Bidi_Class Unicode property.
- [Bidi](https://docs.rs/struct.BidiClassMask.html)- Class - Mask
- A mask representing potentially multiple `BidiClass`values.
- [Joining](https://docs.rs/struct.JoiningType.html)- Type
- Value for the Joining_Type Unicode property.
- [Joining](https://docs.rs/struct.JoiningTypeMask.html)- Type - Mask
- A mask representing potentially multiple `JoiningType`values.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [FIRST_](https://docs.rs/constant.FIRST_BC_MASK.html)- BC_ - MASK
- Mask for allowable bidi classes in the first character of a label (either LTR or RTL) in a bidi domain.
- [LAST_](https://docs.rs/constant.LAST_LTR_MASK.html)- LTR_ - MASK
- [LAST_](https://docs.rs/constant.LAST_RTL_MASK.html)- RTL_ - MASK
- [LEFT_](https://docs.rs/constant.LEFT_OR_DUAL_JOINING_MASK.html)- OR_ - DUAL_ - JOINING_ - MASK
- Mask for checking for both left and dual joining.
- [MIDDLE_](https://docs.rs/constant.MIDDLE_LTR_MASK.html)- LTR_ - MASK
- [MIDDLE_](https://docs.rs/constant.MIDDLE_RTL_MASK.html)- RTL_ - MASK
- [RIGHT_](https://docs.rs/constant.RIGHT_OR_DUAL_JOINING_MASK.html)- OR_ - DUAL_ - JOINING_ - MASK
- Mask for checking for both left and dual joining.
- [RTL_](https://docs.rs/constant.RTL_MASK.html)- MASK
- Mask for checking if the domain is a bidi domain.

---

# idna_adapter - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/idna_adapter/latest/target-redirect/aarch64-apple-darwin/idna_adapter/index.html

## Expand description

This crate abstracts over a Unicode back end for the [ idna](https://docs.rs/crate/idna/latest)
crate.

To work around the lack of [ global-features](https://internals.rust-lang.org/t/pre-rfc-mutually-excusive-global-features/19618) in Cargo, this
crate allows the top level

`Cargo.lock` to choose an alternative
Unicode back end for the `idna` crate by pinning a version of this
crate.See the [README of the latest version](https://docs.rs/crate/idna_adapter/latest) for more details.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Adapter](https://docs.rs/struct.Adapter.html)

- [Bidi](https://docs.rs/struct.BidiClass.html)- Class

- A mask representing potentially multiple `BidiClass`values.

- A mask representing potentially multiple `JoiningType`values.

# Adapter in idna_adapter - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/idna_adapter/latest/target-redirect/aarch64-apple-darwin/idna_adapter/struct.Adapter.html

`pub struct Adapter { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An adapter between a Unicode back end an the `idna` crate.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

`true` iff the Canonical_Combining_Class of `c` is Virama.

`true` iff the General_Category of `c` is Mark, i.e. any of Nonspacing_Mark,
Spacing_Mark, or Enclosing_Mark.

# idna_adapter - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/idna_adapter/1.2.2/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/idna_adapter/

## Expand description

This crate abstracts over a Unicode back end for the [ idna](https://docs.rs/crate/idna/latest)
crate.

To work around the lack of [ global-features](https://internals.rust-lang.org/t/pre-rfc-mutually-excusive-global-features/19618) in Cargo, this
crate allows the top level

`Cargo.lock` to choose an alternative
Unicode back end for the `idna` crate by pinning a version of this
crate.See the [README of the latest version](https://docs.rs/crate/idna_adapter/latest) for more details.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Adapter](https://docs.rs/struct.Adapter.html)
- An adapter between a Unicode back end an the `idna`crate.
- [Bidi](https://docs.rs/struct.BidiClass.html)- Class
- Value for the Bidi_Class Unicode property.
- [Bidi](https://docs.rs/struct.BidiClassMask.html)- Class - Mask
- A mask representing potentially multiple `BidiClass`values.
- [Joining](https://docs.rs/struct.JoiningType.html)- Type
- Value for the Joining_Type Unicode property.
- [Joining](https://docs.rs/struct.JoiningTypeMask.html)- Type - Mask
- A mask representing potentially multiple `JoiningType`values.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [FIRST_](https://docs.rs/constant.FIRST_BC_MASK.html)- BC_ - MASK
- Mask for allowable bidi classes in the first character of a label (either LTR or RTL) in a bidi domain.
- [LAST_](https://docs.rs/constant.LAST_LTR_MASK.html)- LTR_ - MASK
- [LAST_](https://docs.rs/constant.LAST_RTL_MASK.html)- RTL_ - MASK
- [LEFT_](https://docs.rs/constant.LEFT_OR_DUAL_JOINING_MASK.html)- OR_ - DUAL_ - JOINING_ - MASK
- Mask for checking for both left and dual joining.
- [MIDDLE_](https://docs.rs/constant.MIDDLE_LTR_MASK.html)- LTR_ - MASK
- [MIDDLE_](https://docs.rs/constant.MIDDLE_RTL_MASK.html)- RTL_ - MASK
- [RIGHT_](https://docs.rs/constant.RIGHT_OR_DUAL_JOINING_MASK.html)- OR_ - DUAL_ - JOINING_ - MASK
- Mask for checking for both left and dual joining.
- [RTL_](https://docs.rs/constant.RTL_MASK.html)- MASK
- Mask for checking if the domain is a bidi domain.

---

# idna_adapter - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/idna_adapter/latest/target-redirect/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/idna_adapter/index.html

## Expand description

This crate abstracts over a Unicode back end for the [ idna](https://docs.rs/crate/idna/latest)
crate.

To work around the lack of [ global-features](https://internals.rust-lang.org/t/pre-rfc-mutually-excusive-global-features/19618) in Cargo, this
crate allows the top level

`Cargo.lock` to choose an alternative
Unicode back end for the `idna` crate by pinning a version of this
crate.See the [README of the latest version](https://docs.rs/crate/idna_adapter/latest) for more details.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Adapter](https://docs.rs/struct.Adapter.html)
- An adapter between a Unicode back end an the `idna`crate.
- [Bidi](https://docs.rs/struct.BidiClass.html)- Class
- Value for the Bidi_Class Unicode property.
- [Bidi](https://docs.rs/struct.BidiClassMask.html)- Class - Mask
- A mask representing potentially multiple `BidiClass`values.
- [Joining](https://docs.rs/struct.JoiningType.html)- Type
- Value for the Joining_Type Unicode property.
- [Joining](https://docs.rs/struct.JoiningTypeMask.html)- Type - Mask
- A mask representing potentially multiple `JoiningType`values.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [FIRST_](https://docs.rs/constant.FIRST_BC_MASK.html)- BC_ - MASK
- Mask for allowable bidi classes in the first character of a label (either LTR or RTL) in a bidi domain.
- [LAST_](https://docs.rs/constant.LAST_LTR_MASK.html)- LTR_ - MASK
- [LAST_](https://docs.rs/constant.LAST_RTL_MASK.html)- RTL_ - MASK
- [LEFT_](https://docs.rs/constant.LEFT_OR_DUAL_JOINING_MASK.html)- OR_ - DUAL_ - JOINING_ - MASK
- Mask for checking for both left and dual joining.
- [MIDDLE_](https://docs.rs/constant.MIDDLE_LTR_MASK.html)- LTR_ - MASK
- [MIDDLE_](https://docs.rs/constant.MIDDLE_RTL_MASK.html)- RTL_ - MASK
- [RIGHT_](https://docs.rs/constant.RIGHT_OR_DUAL_JOINING_MASK.html)- OR_ - DUAL_ - JOINING_ - MASK
- Mask for checking for both left and dual joining.
- [RTL_](https://docs.rs/constant.RTL_MASK.html)- MASK
- Mask for checking if the domain is a bidi domain.

# Adapter in idna_adapter - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/idna_adapter/latest/target-redirect/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/idna_adapter/struct.Adapter.html

`pub struct Adapter { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An adapter between a Unicode back end an the `idna` crate.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

`true` iff the Canonical_Combining_Class of `c` is Virama.

`true` iff the General_Category of `c` is Mark, i.e. any of Nonspacing_Mark,
Spacing_Mark, or Enclosing_Mark.

# idna_adapter - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/idna_adapter/1.2.2/i686-pc-windows-msvc/idna_adapter/

## Expand description

This crate abstracts over a Unicode back end for the [ idna](https://docs.rs/crate/idna/latest)
crate.

To work around the lack of [ global-features](https://internals.rust-lang.org/t/pre-rfc-mutually-excusive-global-features/19618) in Cargo, this
crate allows the top level

`Cargo.lock` to choose an alternative
Unicode back end for the `idna` crate by pinning a version of this
crate.See the [README of the latest version](https://docs.rs/crate/idna_adapter/latest) for more details.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Adapter](https://docs.rs/struct.Adapter.html)
- An adapter between a Unicode back end an the `idna`crate.
- [Bidi](https://docs.rs/struct.BidiClass.html)- Class
- Value for the Bidi_Class Unicode property.
- [Bidi](https://docs.rs/struct.BidiClassMask.html)- Class - Mask
- A mask representing potentially multiple `BidiClass`values.
- [Joining](https://docs.rs/struct.JoiningType.html)- Type
- Value for the Joining_Type Unicode property.
- [Joining](https://docs.rs/struct.JoiningTypeMask.html)- Type - Mask
- A mask representing potentially multiple `JoiningType`values.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [FIRST_](https://docs.rs/constant.FIRST_BC_MASK.html)- BC_ - MASK
- Mask for allowable bidi classes in the first character of a label (either LTR or RTL) in a bidi domain.
- [LAST_](https://docs.rs/constant.LAST_LTR_MASK.html)- LTR_ - MASK
- [LAST_](https://docs.rs/constant.LAST_RTL_MASK.html)- RTL_ - MASK
- [LEFT_](https://docs.rs/constant.LEFT_OR_DUAL_JOINING_MASK.html)- OR_ - DUAL_ - JOINING_ - MASK
- Mask for checking for both left and dual joining.
- [MIDDLE_](https://docs.rs/constant.MIDDLE_LTR_MASK.html)- LTR_ - MASK
- [MIDDLE_](https://docs.rs/constant.MIDDLE_RTL_MASK.html)- RTL_ - MASK
- [RIGHT_](https://docs.rs/constant.RIGHT_OR_DUAL_JOINING_MASK.html)- OR_ - DUAL_ - JOINING_ - MASK
- Mask for checking for both left and dual joining.
- [RTL_](https://docs.rs/constant.RTL_MASK.html)- MASK
- Mask for checking if the domain is a bidi domain.

---

# Adapter in idna_adapter - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/idna_adapter/latest/target-redirect/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/idna_adapter/struct.Adapter.html

`pub struct Adapter { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An adapter between a Unicode back end an the `idna` crate.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

`true` iff the Canonical_Combining_Class of `c` is Virama.

`true` iff the General_Category of `c` is Mark, i.e. any of Nonspacing_Mark,
Spacing_Mark, or Enclosing_Mark.
